initiatives.name: Fuel for Growth Transformation Programme
initiatives.summary: A multi-year programme modernising operations, simplifying organisational structure, and reducing fixed costs as a share of net revenue through automation, shared services, and digital capabilities. Fixed costs fell from 21.8% of net revenue in 2023 to 19.4% in 2025, targeting ~19% by end of 2027.

evidence.title: Reorganization into three Areas with Area Presidents
evidence.summary: Reckitt evolved its reporting structure from three business units to three Areas with accountability consolidated behind three Area Presidents, reducing management layers and accelerating decision-making closer to consumers and customers.
evidence.quote: To support this focus, we evolved our reporting structure from three business units to three Areas with accountability now consolidated behind three Area Presidents. We have reduced layers of management and accelerated decision making closer to consumers and customers.

evidence.title: Fuel for Growth structural efficiency programme
evidence.summary: A multi-year programme modernising operations, simplifying organisational structure, and reducing fixed costs as a share of net revenue through automation, shared services, and digital capabilities. Fixed costs fell from 21.8% of net revenue in 2023 to 19.4% in 2025, targeting ~19% by end of 2027.
evidence.quote: The programme remains on track to reduce fixed costs to around 19% by the end of 2027, supported by approximately £1 billion of one-off transformation investment across 2024–2027.

evidence.title: Restructuring costs linked to 2024 strategic transformation
evidence.summary: IFRS operating profit was impacted by £195 million of restructuring and other project costs linked to the Group's 2024 strategic announcements, principally comprising professional advisor fees and severance costs relating to business transformation and portfolio changes.
evidence.quote: IFRS operating profit was also affected by restructuring and other project costs of £195 million linked to the Group strategic announcements in 2024. This principally includes professional advisor fees and severance costs relating to business transformation and portfolio changes.

evidence.title: Fuel for Growth Transformation Programme
evidence.summary: Reckitt is undertaking a major restructuring and business transformation programme called 'Fuel for Growth', linked to strategic announcements made in 2024. This includes professional advisor fees and severance costs related to business transformation and portfolio changes.
evidence.quote: Restructuring and other project costs of £195 million linked to the Group strategic announcements in 2024 of which £179 million relates to the Fuel for Growth programme. This principally includes professional advisor fees and severance costs relating to business transformation and portfolio changes

evidence.title: Shared services hubs for finance, IT&D, supply and HR
evidence.summary: Reckitt is rolling out standardised, end-to-end processes across finance, IT&D, supply and HR, underpinned by shared service hubs in Warsaw, Mexico City and Hyderabad, to improve consistency, speed and standardisation as part of Fuel for Growth.
evidence.quote: Work is underway to roll out fully standardised, end-to-end processes across finance, IT&D, supply and HR. They are underpinned by shared service hubs in Warsaw, Mexico City and Hyderabad, which operate as an extension of the markets they support.

initiatives.name: Essential Home Business Divestment
initiatives.summary: Reckitt completed the sale of its Essential Home business (Air Wick, Calgon, Cillit Bang, Mortein, Easy-Off, Woolite, ~75 brands) to private equity firm Advent International on 31 December 2025, retaining a 30% equity stake. This simplifies the portfolio and sharpens focus on high-growth, high-margin Powerbrands.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £2,172 million total consideration (net of disposal costs); £1,786 million net proceeds

evidence.title: Divestment of Essential Home Business
evidence.summary: Reckitt completed the divestment of its Essential Home business on 31 December 2025, retaining a 30% equity stake in the divested entity. Excess cash from the transaction was returned to shareholders via a special dividend.
evidence.quote: As announced on the 31 December 2025, Reckitt agreed the divestment of its Essential Home business with excess cash being returned to shareholders by means of a special dividend of 235 pence per ordinary share.

evidence.title: Divestment of Essential Home to Advent International
evidence.summary: Reckitt completed the sale of its Essential Home business (Air Wick, Calgon, Cillit Bang, Mortein, Easy-Off, Woolite, ~75 brands) to private equity firm Advent International on 31 December 2025, retaining a 30% equity stake. This simplifies the portfolio and sharpens focus on high-growth, high-margin Powerbrands.
evidence.quote: The divestment of Essential Home represents a significant step forward in unlocking substantial value within the Group. It moves Reckitt towards becoming a simpler, more effective world-class consumer health and hygiene company and enables sharper focus on our core portfolio of high-growth, high-margin Powerbrands.

initiatives.name: Net Zero and Sustainability Commitments
initiatives.summary: Reckitt has committed to net zero across its value chain by 2040, including a 65% reduction in GHG emissions in operations by 2030 and 100% renewable electricity by 2030, with 97% already achieved from renewable sources.

evidence.title: Net zero by 2040 across value chain
evidence.summary: Reckitt has committed to net zero across its value chain by 2040, including a 65% reduction in GHG emissions in operations by 2030 and 100% renewable electricity by 2030, with 97% already achieved from renewable sources.
evidence.quote: Net zero across our value chain by 2040 Note 4... 65% reduction in GHG emissions in operations by 20302 100% renewable electricity by 2030... 97% of electricity comes from renewable sources through on-site generation, Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), Green Tariffs and Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs).

evidence.title: Net Zero by 2040 and 2030 GHG Reduction Targets
evidence.summary: Reckitt has committed to achieving net zero across its value chain by 2040, with validated near-term targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 65% and Scope 3 emissions by 50% by 2030 (vs 2015 baseline). The company has already surpassed its Scope 1 and 2 target, achieving a 73% reduction.
evidence.quote: Our ambition is to achieve net zero across our value chain (excluding indirect consumer use emissions) by 2040. ... Reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 65% by 2030, from a 2015 base year (aligned to a 1.5°C pathway) ... We have surpassed our Scope 1 and 2 reduction target, achieving 73% reduction vs 2015 and will review future targets as part of the upcoming SBTi review in 2026.

initiatives.name: Generative AI and Digital Transformation Deployment
initiatives.summary: Reckitt built an internal proprietary generative AI tool for consumer insights and concept generation, rolled out to 12 markets across three areas in 2025. The tool delivers a 70% reduction in concept generation time (up from 60% in 2024) and twice the quality of output.

evidence.title: Generative AI tool for consumer insights and concept generation
evidence.summary: Reckitt built an internal proprietary generative AI tool for consumer insights and concept generation, rolled out to 12 markets across three areas in 2025. The tool delivers a 70% reduction in concept generation time (up from 60% in 2024) and twice the quality of output.
evidence.quote: We have built an internal proprietary Reckitt tool to help us with consumer insights and consumer concept generation, which has now been rolled out to 12 markets across our three areas in 2025... delivering a 70% reduction in time, improving on the 60% achieved in 2024, and twice the quality of output when it is used.

evidence.title: Digital and generative AI deployment across core processes
evidence.summary: Reckitt is deploying digital and generative AI capabilities across core business processes beyond marketing, including R&D and early pilots in forecasting and supply chain diagnostics, alongside ongoing SAP modernisation for standardised global processes.
evidence.quote: These capabilities are now being deployed across core business processes and are already embedded into ways of working in marketing. The same approach is being applied in R&D, while early pilots in forecasting and supply chain diagnostics are demonstrating potential for greater accuracy... SAP modernisation is also progressing, enabling more standardised global processes.

initiatives.name: Share Buyback Programme
initiatives.summary: Reckitt conducted a significant share repurchase programme during 2025, spending £879 million, with further purchases continuing into 2026 and 30 million shares cancelled from Treasury. This represents a capital allocation/portfolio strategy signal, returning capital to shareholders.

evidence.title: Share Buyback Programme
evidence.summary: Reckitt conducted a significant share repurchase programme during 2025, spending £879 million, with further purchases continuing into 2026 and 30 million shares cancelled from Treasury. This represents a capital allocation/portfolio strategy signal, returning capital to shareholders.
evidence.quote: the financial year ended 31 December 2025 was £879 million. A further 921,790 shares have been purchased between 1 January 2026 and 30 January 2026 at a cost of £56 million. Under authority granted to Directors under section 729 of CA 2006 to cancel shares held in Treasury, 30,000,000 ordinary 10 pence shares were cancelled from Treasury on 15 December 2025.

initiatives.name: Biofreeze Impairment and Portfolio Rationalization
initiatives.summary: Reckitt recorded a £175 million impairment charge on Biofreeze due to declining short and medium-term category growth rates, reflecting portfolio performance challenges within Core Reckitt.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £175 million impairment (Biofreeze); £250 million total intangible impairment

evidence.title: Biofreeze intangible asset impairment amid declining category
evidence.summary: Reckitt recorded a £175 million impairment charge on Biofreeze due to declining short and medium-term category growth rates, reflecting portfolio performance challenges within Core Reckitt.
evidence.quote: IFRS operating profit was also impacted by an intangible assets impairment charge of £250 million relating to Biofreeze and other non-software intangible assets (2024: £838 million).
